worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 60,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions, PIT-ADJ line 1 (all state and municipal bond interest left out of federal AGI): other states' bond interest 5,000.00 = 5,000.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 60,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 60,000.00 + 5,000.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 49,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 44,250.00 + 5,000.00 = 49,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 49,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 17,000.00 = 731 + 4.7% x 15,750.00 = 740.25; total 1,905.75, to the cent 1,905.75. The table row over 49,200 to 49,300 gives 1,906; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,905.75.
